text:
sara_se: Paging — Polaris (enterprise) on Private VPC reporting a spike of 502s for prod, started ~14:02 UTC. Customer impact: model responses failing for a subset of requests, affects all prod instances in us-west-2. Can oncall triage?
incident-bot: ALERT: 502 spike detected for tenant=polaris-prod, metric=backend_5xx_rate, threshold=0.05, started=2025-11-05T14:03:22Z :rotating_light:
emma_oncall: I'm on it. Paging netops. @raj_netops can you check NLB/ALB healthchecks and SGs? Need a quick customer-impact summary for SRE lead.
raj_netops: Looking now. Quick glance: NLB target group shows ~50% unhealthy, ALB backend returns 502s. Pulling recent SG audit and conntrack stats.
mike_sre: From service logs — lots of connection resets from NLB IPs, healthcheck `/hc` returning 502. Saw a model rollout at ~13:55 that increased request payload sizes. Could be upstream timeouts or conntrack exhaustion.
polaris-cust-eng: Confirmed on our side — errors spike at 14:02 UTC. No changes to security groups from our ops team. We did push a model change earlier.
sara_se: Customer confirms no SG changes. They did a model rollout that increases avg request size + concurrency. Might be hitting NAT/conn limits or backend timeouts.
raj_netops: Hypothesis: ephemeral port exhaustion / conntrack limit on tenant subnet NAT -> upstream connections dropping, manifests as 502. Quick mitigation: temporarily relax egress SG for the app subnet to allow ephemeral ports to public NAT to reduce connection failures. Will propose scoped rule and expiry.
emma_oncall: Go ahead with a tightly-scoped temporary rule, coordinate with SE & customer. @polaris-cust-eng can you approve a short-lived egress loosen for triage?
polaris-cust-eng: Approve for 10 minutes for triage :thumbsup:
raj_netops: Applying rule now per runbook step 3. Command used: `aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0polarisapp --protocol tcp --port 1024-65535 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0 --region us-west-2` — will auto-expire via scheduled revoke at +15m.
incident-bot: ACTION: egress rule added by raj_netops at 2025-11-05T14:07:10Z (scheduled revoke 14:22Z). Monitoring metrics and healthchecks.
mike_sre: Observing improvement — backend_5xx_rate dropped from 0.18 -> 0.04 over 2m, connection resets decreased. Looks like conntrack/NAT was the issue. :tada:
emma_oncall: Good. Need a permanent remediation plan: NAT GW scaling or client concurrency throttling. Thoughts?
raj_netops: Next steps: provision additional NAT GW for the tenant subnet, add conntrack usage dashboards & alert, and update rollout checklist to warn on payload/concurrency increases. Will schedule infra change after customer approval.
sara_se: I'll send Polaris a short post-incident note with recommended mitigations and the rollback window. We'll roll back the temporary rule after verifying stability.
incident-bot: RESOLVE: incident ticket INC-2025-789 marked mitigated at 2025-11-05T14:14:00Z after egress workaround stabilized traffic. Follow-up: SE/NetOps postmortem and customer remediation checklist.
emma_oncall: Rolling back temporary rule to validate stability. Command: `aws ec2 revoke-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0polarisapp --protocol tcp --port 1024-65535 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0 --region us-west-2`
raj_netops: Rollback complete at 14:20Z. Metrics stable: backend_5xx_rate=0.03, target health=healthy. Marking incident mitigated. :white_check_mark:
polaris-cust-eng: Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick help. We'll throttle request concurrency and schedule NAT GW addition with your infra team.
mike_sre: Adding follow-ups to postmortem: add conntrack dashboard, nat-gw autoscale runbook, model-rollout checklist update (payload size & concurrency guardrails).
